title: The ring, Tuesday
logline: Tuesday. Gully's. The ring on her hand on the counter, drawn as a dot. Gully sees a ring. Wood sees a cup. Gully says 'nice ring.' Wood says 'what ring.' Chloe lets them.

panels.composition: Gully's. CHLOE at the counter, left hand flat on it. On the hand: a dot. GULLY. WOOD on the stool. BARNABY, thirteen, beneath.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a woman with her left hand flat on a bait-shop counter, a tiny dot on one finger, a stocky man in an apron looking at it, a thin man on a stool looking elsewhere, an old dog beneath

panels.composition: Her hand. The dot. Gully's thick finger pointing at it, not touching.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, close-up of a woman's hand on a wooden counter with a tiny dot on the ring finger and a thick finger pointing at it

panels.composition: Wood, looking at the coffee, not the hand.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a thin man on a stool deliberately looking at a coffee cup while a stocky man points at a woman's hand

panels.composition: Chloe, letting them. Her face: the thing she does with her mouth when she's decided not to help. The dog's chin on her boot.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a woman with a small deciding-not-to-help expression at a counter while an old dog rests its chin on her boot, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: 'Then it's a saucer.' Chloe doesn't help. The dot.
